questions.question: What is the safest boundary between a learned robotics policy and the physical controller?
options: The policy directly owns motor authority whenever confidence is above 50%.
The policy proposes bounded actions; an independent authority validates and executes them.
The language model also implements the emergency stop.
The controller accepts every syntactically valid action.
questions.explanation: A probabilistic policy may propose actions, but independent runtime and hardware controls must own the execution envelope.

questions.question: A supervisory loop has a 180 ms deadline and requires 45 ms of response reserve. What is the largest acceptable p95 sense-to-command latency?
options: 180 ms
225 ms
45 ms
135 ms
questions.explanation: The computed path must leave the 45 ms reserve unused: 180 - 45 = 135 ms.

questions.question: Why is model confidence alone a weak runtime safety monitor?
options: The model and its confidence estimate can fail from the same unsupported input or representation error.
Confidence can only be computed in simulation.
Confidence always makes inference too slow.
A confidence score directly measures stopping distance.
questions.explanation: A self-check shares common causes with the policy. Independent freshness, force, geofence, and hardware signals cover different failure paths.

questions.question: Which deployment choice most directly adds network delay and jitter to the action path?
options: Reducing the robot payload
Recording a local incident trace
Serving the policy from a remote model endpoint
Adding a mechanical brake
questions.explanation: Remote inference can add both round-trip delay and a wider latency tail, so local fallback behavior remains necessary.

questions.question: What should happen when a camera frame is older than the action gate's freshness boundary?
options: Increase the proposed speed to catch up.
Reuse the previous command indefinitely.
Hold motion, reacquire evidence, and replan.
Disable the timestamp check.
questions.explanation: A stale observation no longer justifies the proposal. The safe response is to stop extending that plan and obtain current evidence.

questions.question: Which evaluation sequence best manages the sim-to-real evidence gap?
options: Simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, guarded bench tests, then staged operating-domain trials
One successful simulation followed by unrestricted deployment
Text benchmark scores followed by a product launch
Only aggregate task-success testing
questions.explanation: Each stage exposes failure modes the previous environment cannot represent while limiting the cost of discovery.

questions.question: Why must an incident trace include model, calibration, controller, and firmware versions?
options: To make the log file larger
To avoid recording sensor timestamps
To replace physical inspection
To reconstruct the executable policy and the exact authority path that produced motion
questions.explanation: The deployed behavior is produced by the whole executable stack, not only the learned checkpoint.

questions.question: When can teleoperation be the wrong immediate fallback?
options: Whenever the task has more than one step
When operator connection and takeover latency exceed the physical hazard window
When the robot has a camera
When a model runs on-device
questions.explanation: A handoff that arrives after the hazard window cannot be the first containment action; the robot needs a local safe response.
